title: KMS ops: rotation checklist, SIEM export & evidence flow
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact operational cheat-sheet for key management (KMS/HSM/BYOK), rotation procedures, and the SIEM / evidence flow used by Security and Ops. Intended for on-call engineers, SREs, and security engineers who execute rotations or respond to key incidents.

Scope and assumptions:
- Covers Redwood-managed KEKs (HSM-backed root), customer BYOK onboarding basics, tenant key rotation cadence, and evidence export to SIEM.
- Assumes envelope encryption: Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) are generated per tenant/workload and wrapped by Key Encryption Keys (KEKs) in a KMS/HSM.
- This doc focuses on operational steps and SIEM mapping; for formal compliance artifacts see the KMS runbook in Confluence.

High-level architecture (for quick mental model):
- Root HSM Cluster (FIPS-validated HSM) holds master root keys; limited admins, no application access.
- Platform KMS (internal service) manages KEKs, interacts with HSM for cryptographic operations.
- Tenant BYOK connectors (external KMS endpoints) for customers who bring keys; Redwood stores only references and uses remote wrap/unwrap where configured.
- DEKs: short-lived per-workload keys (rotated more frequently), encrypted with KEKs.

RBAC v2 mapping (who can do what) — recommended minimal set for rotation ops:
- security-admin: full KMS config, HSM admin, key creation/deletion, role management (limit to 3 people).
- kms-operator: schedule rotations, trigger key rewraps, kick off validation jobs.
- kms-reader / auditor: read-only access to key metadata and audit events, cannot unwrap.
- tenant-admin: limited to tenant-level key operations (create/revoke tenant keys) only if BYOK is enabled and tenant has explicit consent configured.

RBAC tips:
- Use scoped service accounts for automation (no interactive human creds).
- Enforce short-lived credentials (OIDC or similar) for operator sessions.
- Log RBAC changes to audit channel and require 2-person review for promotion to security-admin.

Key types and recommended lifecycles:
- Root key (HSM-kept): rotate rarely (3–5 years), emergency work only.
- Platform KEK: rotate yearly for policy-bound keys; rewrap DEKs during maintenance windows.
- Tenant KEKs (BYOK): follow customer contract; if customer requests rotation, coordinate and record consent.
- DEKs: rotate on workload deploys or on schedule (default 90 days).

Pre-rotation checklist (run before any rotation):
1) Confirm maintenance window and stakeholder notify list (list in Confluence).
2) Snapshot current key metadata (key IDs, versions, creation dates) and export to evidence bucket.
3) Run compatibility test suite against target models/workloads (scripts in infra-scripts/kms-tests).
4) Ensure cross-region replicas and periodic backup snapshots are healthy.
5) Verify SIEM pipeline is green; ensure forwarding to Splunk/Elastic is healthy.
6) Verify rollback plan & test restore procedure in a staging environment.

Rotation procedure — typical KEK rewrap (high-level steps):
A) Trigger key version creation (create new KEK version in KMS; HSM signs new key blob).
B) Rewrap DEKs: iterate over DEK manifests and call Rewrap(DEK, oldKEK->newKEK) in batches.
   - Prefer continuous, streaming rewrap with throttling (avoid large concurrency spikes).
   - Default batch size: 200 DEKs / 60s; adjust by observed latency.
C) Validate rewrap: sanity-check sample decrypt/encrypt operations per tenant.
D) Promote new KEK version to active (update metadata and routing).
E) Mark old KEK version deprecated, schedule deletion after retention window (e.g., 30 days).

Commands and example (pseudo):
- create-new-key-version --key-id=projects/p/keys/ke1
- list-dek-manifests --key=ke1 --since=2025-01-01 | rewrap-batcher --target-key-version=ke1-v2
- validate-rewrap --sample-tenants=50 --concurrency=5

Post-rotation validation checklist:
- Verify no error spikes in matching SLO dashboards (encryption-errors, unwrap-latency).
- Confirm sample test decrypts succeed for each tenant category (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Export evidence report: key-metadata-before.json, key-metadata-after.json, rewrap-job-log-<id>.txt to evidence bucket.
- Open ticket SEC-RETRO-YYYYMM for retrospective if any anomalies.

Emergency key compromise playbook (abridged):
1) If an HSM/KEK compromise suspected, immediately set KEK status to revoked (keeps existing ciphertext but prevents new unwraps).
2) Switch to emergency fallback KEK (pre-provisioned and securely stored in HSM backup cluster).
3) Kick off urgent full rewrap of DEKs to the emergency KEK; prioritize high-sensitivity tenancies first.
4) Notify legal/compliance and customers per SLA/contract.
5) Preserve all logs and evidence artifacts (sequester and snapshot SIEM events).
6) Conduct root cause analysis and full audit.

Evidence automation & SIEM export details:
- Evidence artifacts to collect automatically for every rotation:
  - key_metadata_before.json (list of keys, versions, owners)
  - key_metadata_after.json
  - rotation_job_<id>.log (stdout/stderr)
  - sample_decrypt_results_<id>.csv
  - rollforward_checksums_<id>.sha256
- Automation jobs: infra-scripts/kms-ops/rotate-and-collect.sh (cron: 0 3 * * 0 for non-prod test run), production runs via CD pipeline.
- SIEM export: events are forwarded via syslog-ng to our Splunk indexer and also to Elastic for cross-correlation. Forwarded events must include a canonical event schema (see below).

Canonical audit log schema (SIEM-friendly flat field set):
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- event_type: one of [key.create,key.rotate,key.rewrap,key.revoke,key.delete,key.access,key.unwrap,key.wrap,rbac.change]
- event_id: UUID
- request_id: platform request id
- key_id: canonical key identifier (ke-xxxx or tenant-ke-yyy)
- key_version: string
- operation: free text (e.g., RewrapBatch, CreateKeyVersion)
- principal: user/service principal email or service account id
- principal_role: RBAC role at time of op
- src_ip: IP address of caller (if applicable)
- region: region tag of target key/DEK
- result: success | failure | partial
- error_code: if any (short code)
- latency_ms: integer
- sample_count: for batch operations, number processed
- evidence_refs: comma-separated list of artifact URIs (s3:// or gs://)
- notes: free text (short)

Example line (newline-delimited JSON string stored in SIEM raw event):
{"timestamp":"2025-03-01T08:15:32Z","event_type":"key.rewrap","event_id":"8b1f-...","request_id":"req-4823","key_id":"ke-prod-87","key_version":"v2","operation":"RewrapBatch","principal":"svc-kms-operator@redwood.ai","principal_role":"kms-operator","src_ip":"10.12.34.56","region":"us-west1","result":"success","latency_ms":2314,"sample_count":200,"evidence_refs":"gs://redwood-evidence/kms/rotate/2025-03-01/before.json,gs://redwood-evidence/kms/rotate/2025-03-01/after.json","notes":"batch 5/23"}

SIEM mapping tips:
- Ensure deduplication uses event_id; tags should include key_id for easy pivots.
- Forward both raw events and aggregated metrics (per-hour counts of key.access failures).
- Use saved searches for suspicious patterns: repeated unwrap failures across many principals; unexpected key_version changes outside scheduled windows.

Retention and evidence handling:
- Keep rotation evidence in evidence bucket for 2 years for enterprise customers; for others 1 year.
- Apply immutable blob/retention policy on evidence artifacts after collection.
- Archive proofs for compliance requests via secure export (signed manifest file).

Operational FAQs / quick answers:
Q: Can we delete an old KEK version immediately after rotation?
A: No — retain for a minimum quarantine window (30 days) to allow rollback and for compliance evidence. Delete only after secure deletion process and approval.

Q: Who authorizes BYOK needle rotations requested by a tenant?
A: Tenant-owner + Security ops approval; record consent in ticket and in evidence bundle.

Q: How do we handle BYOK failures when external KMS is unreachable?
A: Failover to cached wrapped DEK only if allowed by tenant policy. Otherwise mark tenant impact and follow outage playbook.

Where to find related resources (quick links):
- Confluence KMS runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/KMS+Operations+Home
- Rotation scripts repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra-scripts.git (kms-ops folder)
- Evidence bucket (read-only): gs://redwood-evidence/kms/
- Incident template: https://redwood.atlassian.net/secure/IssuetypeCreate!init.jspa?issuetype=Incident

Open questions / future work (notes-to-self):
- Add automated rewrap progress dashboards (percent complete, ETA) to Console.
- Expand automated tests to cover cross-region rewrap edge cases.
- Formalize BYOK consent flow into a signed webhook between tenant and Vault.

If you run a rotation or an emergency action using this cheat-sheet: drop notes into the SEC-ops Slack channel, tag @security-oncall, and attach the evidence_refs created by automation.

-- end of cheat-sheet --
